findings.title: Priority inversion on a condition variable: rtdemo[15847445] likely waits for P-producer
findings.explanation: rtdemo[15847445] 'A-control' waits on a condition variable. Nobody owns a condition variable, so QNX cannot raise the thread that will signal it to the waiter's priority. rtdemo[15847445] 'P-producer' (priority 10) was ready to run but rtdemo[15847445] 'B-worker' (priority 20) had its CPU; if it is the thread that signals, the waiter waits for the middle-priority thread. This is a priority inversion without a lock.
evidence: rtdemo[15847445] 'A-control' (priority 30) was blocked on a condition variable in 13 of 17 snapshots (sync object 0x485a1ba018).

In 7 of those, rtdemo[15847445] 'P-producer' (priority 10), a thread of the same process below the waiter, was READY but not running, while rtdemo[15847445] 'B-worker' (priority 20) ran on its CPU (CPU 1).
The deadline report for A-control shows 678 misses in 110 run(s) of consecutive misses; 110 started with a long wait in the task's synchronisation step (worst 44.4 ms).
could_not_determine: Which thread will signal the condition variable: it has no owner, so this is the likeliest candidate (same process, below the waiter, held off its CPU), not a proven one. A kernel trace (--trace) can show whether each wait ends right after it runs.
A worst case: finite runs cannot prove the deadline will always be met after a fix.
findings.suggested_fix: There is no priority inheritance on a condition variable, and PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT on its mutex does not change that. Run the signalling thread above the middle-priority work (now 10 vs 20); or let the waiter do the work itself; or ask for it with MsgSend from a server, which on QNX runs at its client's priority.

limits: The trace does not name the condition variable or semaphore, or who signals it (THCONDVAR and THSEM only name the waiter); the candidate comes from the snapshots, and the trace shows whether each wait ends while it runs.
The trace covers 1001 ms of the run; it shows what happened in that window only.
